root_cause.text: In `ets_qdisc_change()`, when a class transitions from DRR (quantum) mode to strict mode, the code fails to remove the class from the DRR active list, causing a double add when the class later reverts to DRR mode.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "Whenever a user issues an ets qdisc change command, transforming a drr class into a strict one, the ets code isn't checking whether that class was in the active list and removing it." The patch adds a loop at line 664 that explicitly deletes the class from the active list (`list_del_init`) for classes that become strict, confirming the missing removal. The splat with `list_add double add` confirms the resulting list corruption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing cleanup of class list membership when strict band count is increased in ETS qdisc.
intent_record.what: Added a for loop from i = q->nstrict to i < nstrict that calls list_del_init on q->classes[i].alist if the class is active.
intent_record.how: During ETS qdisc reconfiguration, when the number of strict bands is increased, this loop removes any active classes in the newly strict range from their current list (alist), preventing them from lingering in an inappropriate scheduling list.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing cleanup of class list membership when strict band count is increased in ETS qdisc.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent directly addresses the missing cleanup of class list membership when transitioning to strict mode, which is the exact root cause of the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: Updating the number of strict bands without first removing any now-strict classes from the DRR active list causes them to remain on the list. When a class later reverts to DRR mode, it will be added again, resulting in a double-add.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement updates the number of strict bands without removing now-strict classes from the DRR active list. When a class later reverts to DRR mode, it is added again, causing a double-add bug.
